study.title: Acts 20: Farewell, pastoral care and the value of grace
study.overview: Acts 20 shows Paul in motion among churches that he had served, but the center of the chapter is not only his journey: it is his dedication to the spiritual good of the disciples. The account alternates scenes of communion, prolonged teaching, intervention of God in the life of Itism and, finally, the farewell with the elders of Ephesus. The chapter highlights a leadership marked by humility, tears, complete teaching, honest work, vigilance against false teachers and confidently surrender of the church to God and to the word of his grace. The final farewell is painful because Paul announces that he will not see them again, making the affection between pastor and church visible and deep.

outline.title: Trips between Macedonia, Greece and Asia
outline.explanation: Paul leaves Ephesus after the turmoil, strengthens the disciples in the regions where he passes and goes back to Macedonia. The text shows an itinerant ministry, attentive to the churches and also the collection for those in need in Jerusalem, although this appears in the notes as an interpretive backdrop.

outline.title: The meeting in Troas and the Resurrection of Uthic
outline.explanation: On the first day of the week, the disciples gather to break the bread, and Paul teaches until the dawn. A young man falls from the window and is given as dead, but Paul embraces him and God returns him to life, bringing comfort to the church.

outline.title: The route to Miletus and the haste to Jerusalem
outline.explanation: Paul's companions follow by ship, as he walks to Assos and then continues to Miletus. Paul avoids spending time in Ephesus because he wants to reach Jerusalem in time for Pentecost, if this is possible for him.

outline.title: The speech to the elders of Ephesus and the farewell
outline.explanation: Paul recalls his humble service, his public and domestic teaching, his call to repentance and faith, and his willingness to suffer for the gospel. Then he exhorts the leaders to take care of themselves and the flock, warns of cruel wolves and recommends the church to the grace of God. The chapter ends with prayer, tears and the anguish of definitive separation.

study.context: The chapter takes place at the end of a stage of Paul's ministry, after the turmoil in Ephesus and before his trip to Jerusalem. The text mentions displacements by Macedonia, Greece, Asia, Troas, Assos, Mythylene, Chios, Samos, Miletus and Ephesus. The notes highlight that Paul was on a pastoral journey between churches and that his stop at Miletus was strategic to say goodbye to the elders of Ephesus without stopping in the city itself.
study.theology: Acts 20 emphasizes that Christian ministry is service, not self-promotion. Paul serves the Lord with humility, tears and perseverance; preaches repentance to God and faith in Jesus Christ; and he views bonds and afflictions without considering his own life as something precious above the mission received. The chapter also teaches that the church belongs to God and was acquired at a very high price, so its leaders should watch closely. The language of the text on the blood of God, understood by many as a reference to the redemptive work of Christ, underlines the value of the church and the seriousness of the pastoral call. Moreover, the Christian community appears as a place of continuous teaching, worship, communion, prayer and comfort. The resurrection of Ittics shows the power of God acting in human weakness and confirms that the gospel brings life where death was. The final farewell unites doctrine and affection: fidelity to truth and pastoral love do not contradict each other.

scholarViews.insight: Paul remained in Macedonia strengthening the believers in the cities and continuing to organize the offer for the needy in Jerusalem, with special attention to the support of the churches.
The meeting of the disciples on the first day of the week shows the regular practice of worship in common, and not just individual devotion, to maintain communion with God and among the brethren.
The expression of not having ceased to announce all the counsel of God is understood as the integral preaching of revealed truth for salvation, without omitting what could be useful to souls.

questions: What, in Paul's life, shows that Christian fidelity includes both doctrinal firmness and tears and personal care?
How does the warning to the elders of Ephesus correct superficial visions of leadership in the church?
How can Paul's farewell help us to value the communion of the church without transforming emotional attachment at the centre of faith?
study.practice: This chapter calls the church to cultivate a humble, transparent and vigilant leadership. Leaders and members should examine their lives, resist greed, work honestly when necessary, support the fragile and remember that the gospel is to be announced throughout. We are also urged to treat the communion of the church as something precious: to listen to the Word with perseverance, to pray together, to comfort those who suffer and to send us away from each other with sincere love. In practice, this means serving without seeking advantage, teaching with integrity, protecting the community from errors and entrusting the church to God rather than to human force.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided bring some interpretive readings, such as the reference to the collection for Jerusalem in 1-2 and the identification of certain cities as relevant on trade routes; these observations are not developed by the biblical text itself. The expression of 20:28 about the church of God acquired through his own blood is theologically significant, but admits different confessing Christian readings as to the exact way of relating this phrase to the person of Christ. It is also not possible, only with the text and the given notes, to determine with certainty all the internal historical details of the composition of Acts or the exact extent of the ecclesiastical organization of Ephesus.
